title: Conversion hooks: per-item data conversion for a destructive schema change, no acknowledgment token needed
body: Schema-engine rebuild Phase 7 (owner-approved rule-6, 2026-07-24): a destructive item a conversion hook resolves needs NO acknowledgment token -- authoring the hook IS the acknowledgment. Use this instead of `-AcknowledgeDestructive` when a change needs real data conversion (e.g. splitting one column's meaning into another), not just a blind drop. Workflow: (1) See the blast radius BEFORE deploying: `Build-NpdevApp.ps1 -ImpactOnly` (builds + runs the jar once against the target's LIVE database with npdev.schema.lifecycle.mode=REPORT_ONLY, zero writes, exits 0/2/3) or the ControlPanel `GET /api/admin/schema-migration/impact` (SUPERUSER). Each item prints its `itemKey`, e.g. `DROP_COLUMN:products:price_cents:INTEGER`. (2) Write a hook folder in the APP DEFINITION (layer 2): `definition/migrations/<ordinal>-<slug>/hook.json` + `convert.sql` (+ optional `convert.h2.sql`/`convert.postgres.sql`). `hook.json`: `id` (also the destination folder name AND the natural-sort execution order -- prefix it with the same ordinal as the folder, e.g. `"001-split-price"`), `claims` (array of itemKeys this hook resolves), optional `description`/`verifySql`/`verifyExpect` (default 0). `convert.sql` does the REAL work including the destructive DDL itself -- it is not a pre-step the platform re-executes. (3) Regenerate: `ConversionHookEmitter` validates hook.json against `NPDevContract/schemas/conversion-hook.schema.json` at GENERATION time (a malformed hook fails the BUILD, never the boot) and copies valid hooks to `src/main/resources/db/conversion-hooks/<id>/`. (4) Re-run `-ImpactOnly` -- the claimed item now shows `HOOK: <id>` instead of `!!`, and if that was the only destructive item the verdict drops from DESTRUCTIVE to SAFE with no token shown. Still read-only. (5) Deploy for real: `ConversionHookRunner` (invoked from `SchemaLifecycleExecutor.beforeMigrateDecision`, right before the destructive decision) runs every hook whose claims match the live unresolved diff, in ascending natural `id` order, each in its OWN transaction, runs `verifySql` if set (mismatch -> abort BEFORE anything destructive, `HOOK_VERIFY_FAILED`), then re-diffs to confirm the claim was actually honored (a claim still present after the hook ran -> refuse the boot, never trust without checking). Every step writes an `npdev_schema_history` row. An item NO hook claims is completely unaffected -- it stays exactly as token-gated as before Phase 7. Gotcha: `ConversionHookRunner` lives in `com.finalexec.db`, NOT `com.finalexec.db.schemastate` as an early plan sketch suggested -- that subpackage has no access to the package-private `ShadowParityProbe.scopeToOwnedBusinessTables` diff-scoping every other Impact Report surface uses. Phase 8 companion: `ImpactReport`/`ImpactReportJson`'s `proposedConversionSql` field now drafts a copy-convert SQL script (ADD temp column, UPDATE via SUBSTRING for a varchar shrink or CAST otherwise, DROP the old column, RENAME the temp one into place) for a convertible narrowing -- paste it as a starting point for `convert.sql`, but NEVER auto-run; omitted (null) for an incompatible cross-family cast (e.g. VARCHAR->INTEGER), which needs a hand-written hook. v1 is SQL-only; a Java `DataMigrationHook` is deferred to ADR-0003.
